Cluster Snapshots

1. What are Cluster Snapshots?
  • A snapshot is a consistent, point-in-time copy of all persistent caches in the cluster;
  • Snapshots can be used for backup, disaster recovery, or migrating data between clusters;
  • Available since Ignite 2.9; requires Native Persistence to be enabled;
2. Creating a Snapshot
  • Via control script: 
    $IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --snapshot create my_snapshot
  • Programmatically: 
    ignite.snapshot().createSnapshot("my_snapshot").get();
  • Snapshots are taken online — no downtime required;
  • Each node stores its local portion of the snapshot in the snapshot directory;
3. Restoring from a Snapshot
  • Via control script: 
    # Restore all caches
$IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --snapshot restore my_snapshot

# Restore specific caches
$IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --snapshot restore my_snapshot --caches cache1,cache2
  • Programmatically: 
    ignite.snapshot().restoreSnapshot("my_snapshot", null).get();
  • The caches being restored must not exist in the cluster (destroy them first);
4. Snapshot Validation
  • Verify snapshot integrity before restoring: 
    $IGNITE_HOME/bin/control.sh --snapshot check my_snapshot
  • This validates partition checksums and ensures the snapshot is consistent;
5. Snapshot Storage
  • By default, snapshots are stored in $IGNITE_WORK_DIR/snapshots/;
  • Configure a custom path: 
    storageCfg.setSnapshotPath("/mnt/backups/ignite-snapshots");
  • Each snapshot is a directory containing partition files for each node — you can copy them to remote storage for backup;
